title: LibPreemptible: Enabling Fast, Adaptive, and Hardware-Assisted User-Space Scheduling
problem: Modern cloud applications suffer from high tail latencies due to highly-dispersive request distributions, and existing scheduling solutions either require significant OS modifications, have scalability limitations, or fail to utilize full hardware capabilities.
motivation: Reducing tail latencies is critical for cloud application performance and user experience.
method: LibPreemptible creates a thread scheduler that runs inside your application rather than in the operating system kernel. It works through three techniques: the CPU delivers timed signals that interrupt threads so they can be rescheduled; your code supplies custom rules (adaptive scheduling policies) that decide which thread runs next based on current conditions; and the system adjusts these rules automatically. Since the hardware handles the timing, no changes to the OS kernel are needed.
key_novelty: Using the CPU's built-in timed interrupt capability enables efficient preemptive scheduling (interrupting one thread to run another) entirely within applications, without any operating system modifications.
contributions: Fast and lightweight hardware mechanism for timed interrupt delivery to user-space
API for expressing application-specific adaptive scheduling policies
Significant tail latency and throughput improvements over Shinjuku without kernel changes
